name: Staff Pick - Goat's Milk
tagline: You choose the texture & the flavor, we'll choose the cheese!
description: If you are reading this, you like goat's milk cheese. Well, we do too! Here's all you do: just choose the texture, flavor & the amount and we'll do the rest! Based on your answers, we'll choose a cheese that we love and that fits your criteria - couldn't be easier! It's just like standing in front of the cheese case! Feel free to add any specifics in the Instructions/Additions field at checkout. The published price per lb is only a place holder - the exact price of the cheese will be determined by the amount selected and the actual price per lb of the cheese selected

name: L'Abbaye de Bel'loc
tagline: Pasteurized Sheep - L'Abbaye de Bel'loc - Pyrenees, France
description: A beloved Basque sheep cheese, L'Abbaye de Bel'loc was facing extinction only a few years ago. Abbaye Notre-Dame de Bel'loc has been home to Benedictine monks since 1875. In 1959, they decided to start making cheese with milk from their own flock. Their cheese quickly became an international favorite. Unfortunately, by 2018, the monastery was down to only 20 residents and without new priests joining their community to continue their tradition of cheesemaking, they made the difficult decision to stop exporting their cheese. Thanks to the French nonprofit Habitat et Humanisme stepping in and using the abbey to house cheesemaking interns and others struggling with housing issues, we are able to enjoy this cheese again! Dense and silky, this delightful cheese has notes of brown butter, cooked cream, toasted nuts, and pale caramel. Try it and you will understand why we are so excited to have it back!

name: Tomme Corse Brebis
tagline: Pasteurized Sheep - Ottavi - Corsica
description: For 150 years, the Ottavi family's legacy has been passed down from generation to generation with a deep respect for tradition. Nestled in the Fium'Orbu Valley in Haute Corse, they work with the same passion as their ancestors to create cheeses that reflect their land and history. Their cheesemaking adventure began in 1948, when the generation in charge decided to create the Ottavi cheese dairy. From the beginning, everything was handmade and sold directly to locals, door to door. It is this proximity to people and to nature that has forged their identity. In the 1960s, faced with the growing success of their products, they decided to focus exclusively on cheese and maintaining traditional methods. Despite the changes of time, they remain committed to the ancestral practices passed down through the years and continue to produce cheeses with the same care to ensure authenticity. Each cheese is a way for them to extend this family heritage, while sharing a little of the Corsica they love so much. Tomme Corse Brebis is made from sheep’s milk and aged in the Ottavi cellars for three months where it develops its fruity and nutty taste. Excellent as a snack or grated over salads and pasta!

name: Ombra (Ros)
tagline: Pasteurized Sheep - Josep Cuixart - Catalonia, Spain
description: Ombra as it is known in the USA, Ros to the Spaniards, was created by esteemed Spanish cheesemaker Josep Cuixart. The name Ros means "blondie" in Catalan and was chosen to reflect Cuixart's nickname, (due to his fair hair) and the straw color of the cheese's interior when mature. Wheels are about three inches tall, with a natural rind, coated with gray and brown molds. The minimum age is four months, but the cheese can withstand up to ten months of ripening. The interior paste is firm and close-textured and occasionally studded with crunchy nuggets of crystalized amino acids. Flavors are of butterscotch and pineapple, and well balanced between citrus acidity and the sweetness of the milk. Once in hand, all you need is a glass of Rioja.

name: Le Berger Basque
tagline: Raw Sheep - Fermiers Basco Bearnais - Midi-Pyrenees, France
description: Great things come from the Basque region of France & Spain. Among them...breath taking views, iconic cycling climbs & beautifully aged sheep's milk cheeses. Le Berger Basque is a rustic, raw milk example that is a staff favorite. It is at once nutty, earthy, herbaceous and sweet. The paste is dense and creamy, growing more assertive toward the natural rind. If you enjoy other cheeses like Ossau-Iraty or Pyrenees Brebis, you need to add this one to the list!

name: Le Secret de Compostelle
tagline: Pasteurized Sheep - Agour - Pyrenees, France
description: This is a secret you want in on! Produced by Fromagerie Agour, Le Secret de Compostelle is an aged sheep milk cheese in the “brebis Pyrennes” style, similar to Ossau Iraty. Its name pays homage to a passage between the French and Spanish Basque regions, which was commonly traversed by pilgrims on their way to the city of Santiago de Compostela (Compostelle in French). Aged around eight months, this cheese is dense and firm, with a smooth, creamy texture. The natural rind is mildly pungent and savory, while the paste of the offers notes of cream, caramel, nuts, mushrooms, and olives.

name: Adarre
tagline: Pasteurized Goat/Sheep - Rodolphe le Meunier - Pays Basque, France
description: Put simply, this is a spectacular cheese. From the Basque region in France, it is selected by renowned affineur Rodolphe Le Meunier. Like any great recipe, all its components are in balance. Sweet, nutty, bright & tangy, it is the perfect combination of sheep & goat's milk. Add in it's creamy mouthfeel, and you know why Adarre makes every DeLa Deli Team member's Top 5!

name: Bamboozle
tagline: Pasteurized Cow & Goat - Goat Rodeo Farm & Dairy - Pittsburgh, PA
description: India Loevner and her husband, Steve, have owned their 130-acre rural property near Pittsburgh for decades. They raised their children there, with chickens and pigs, but it was never a working farm until India accompanied a friend to a dairy goat show and came home with the two top finishers. Goat Rodeo Farm & Dairy, the inevitable outcome, now makes about a half-dozen cheeses, from fresh chèvre to goat Gouda. Bamboozle is a blend of goat's milk from the Loevners' herd and cow's milk from neighboring farms. Supple, semi-soft texture with notes of prosciutto and peanuts, Bamboozle is aged for at least two months and washed with beer from Cinderlands Beer Co. Equally at home on a cheese board or melted on a burger!

name: Cabra Romero
tagline: Pasteurized Goat - Lorenzo - Murcia, Spain
description: From the Murcia region of Spain, this mild goat cheese receives a coating of rosemary and lard in its final days of aging. Though the rosemary makes this cheese exceedingly herbaceous, it complements, rather than competes with the cheese itself. Murcia is known for its excellent quality of goat’s milk and this cheese is a reflection of it. The paste is ivory white & creamy with a bright, pleasantly piquant flavor.

name: Chabrin
tagline: Pasteurized Goat - Onetik - Macaye, France
description:
From the French Basque Country, Chabrin is a natural rind, pressed cheese made in the traditions of the region using milk from a cooperative of farmers. Each wheel is aged in their cellars, for three months giving the cheese a lovely mineral aroma.

It is mildly goaty with sweet and nutty overtones. The dense, smooth and creamy texture coats the palette and lingers, makes this a very approachable introduction to goats’ milk cheese. Among aged goat cheeses, Chabrin is a DeLaurenti Deli Team favorite!

name: Ciel de Chevre
tagline: Raw Goat - Le Fermiere de Mean - Ardennes, Belgium
description: Modeled on a cow’s milk cheese made by the same producer, Ciel de Chevre is a Trappist style raw goat’s milk cheese. The milk used in this cheese is from a single farm-member of the cooperative. Over the course of 6 weeks, the cheese is washed in a brine solution that gives Ciel de Chevre’s salmon-pink rind its color and helps the ivory white interior develop its flavor and supple texture. The flavor of the semi-soft paste is tangy and savory to the point of meatiness. Its rind is edible and has a crunchy texture and salty flavor.

name: Etorki
tagline: Pasteurized Sheep - Fromagerie des Chaumes - Basque, France
description: Produced at Fromagerie des Chaumes at Mauléon, in southwestern France, Etorki, which means "origin" in local dialect, is a Basque-style sheep's milk cheese. The texture of Etorki is smooth, supple and velvety. The color of the interior paste is a gentle, golden, ivory and there are occasional holes or slits. Aromas are earthy and sweet. Flavors are rich and sweet with notes of hazelnut and caramel.

name: Fleur du Maquis
tagline: Pasteurized Sheep - Ottavi - Corsica
description: Made in Corsica from the milk of Lacaune ewes, this cheese's name translates to "flower of the maquis," the "maquis" being a local term for the typical thickets of rough underbrush where highway robbers and guerrilla fighters used to hang out. This cheese also goes by "Brin d'Amour," meaning "a breath of love." The sheep freely browse Corsica's scrubby, Mediterranean landscape and during production, to enhance the natural flavors present in the milk, the small cheeses are encrusted with rosemary, savory, oregano, marjoram, basil, and thyme. When young, Fleur du Maquis is semi-firm, pliable and moist, with citrus flavors and a pleasant, bright tang. With age the rind becomes dotted with a blue-grey mold. The texture of the cheese also becomes softer, absorbing the savory and herbaceous flavors of the rind. Flavors strike a delicate balance with the herbs, enhancing the warm, bright, sheepy quality of the interior paste. If allowed to mature fully, the paste breaks down and becomes runny and stronger tasting. This cheese pairs well with many types of wines, particularly Tempranillo and Alberino. It's fun to experiment alongside honeys, too; try it with a thyme honey or a floral honey from Corsica.

name: Garrotxa
tagline: Pasteurized Goat - Sant Gil d'Albio - Catalonia, Spain
description: After near extinction in the early 80's, Garrotxa has grown in popularity and demand the last few decades, again becoming one of Spain's most notable goat cheeses. From the Catalan region in southern Spain, Garrotxa is immediately recognized by its powdery, suede-like gray rind. The moist paste is bright white with occasional small holes, or eyes. Flavors are earthy, nutty, and tangy, with a balanced acidity. Pairs well with marcona almonds, dry sherry, Rioja or cava.

name: Hootenanny
tagline: Pasteurized Goat - Goat Rodeo Farm & Dairy - Pittsburgh, PA
description: India Loevner and her husband, Steve, have owned their 130-acre rural property near Pittsburgh for decades. They raised their children there, with chickens and pigs, but it was never a working farm until India accompanied a friend to a dairy goat show and came home with the two top finishers. Goat Rodeo Farm & Dairy, the inevitable outcome, now makes about a half-dozen cheeses, from fresh chèvre to goat Gouda. Hootenanny is their award-winning goat’s milk Gouda cheese made from spring and summer milk. Supple with notes of hickory nuts and wild flowers within a beautiful cream wax rind. Pairs well with crisp white wine or an amber ale.

name: L'Estanguet
tagline: Pasteurized Goat - Les Saloirs de Louis - Basque Country, France
description: Louis Madec began his career as a shepherd before transitioning to aging cheese. Leading his sheep across the high mountain pastures and making cheese in a traditional cauldron gave him an appreciation for livestock farming and cheesemaking. Working with small producers in the valleys of the Upper Béarn, he selects cheeses with an objective of respect for the product, traditions, and the terroir. In addition to those traditional cheeses, he also ages some more innovative styles. L'Estanguet, a semi-firm goat cheese washed with Jurançon wine, is a result of such innovation. Sweet, creamy, tangy and nutty, the complex flavor of this goat tomme has quickly become a staff favorite!

name: La Chevrette
tagline: Pasteurized Goat - Barbichette - Pays Basque, France
description: Part of the Barbichette range from Fromi, La Chevrette is a small goat tomme from the Pays Basque. Ripened for two months, we love its soft texture, distinctive rind, and delicately goaty notes. This Basque treat is the perfect snack for any time of day!

name: La Dama Sagrada
tagline: Raw Goat - MItica - Castilla la Mancha, Spain
description: La Dama Sagrada, or Sacred Dame, is produced using raw Murciana goat’s milk in the town of El Carpio de Tajo in the Castile-La Mancha Region. Made using the molds of a Manchego, the rind has the characteristic basket-weave pattern. With a minimum of 6 months aging, the paste develops a slightly dry yet chewy texture. The flavor is a balance of tang and grass with warm notes of toasted coconut.

name: Manchego 12 month DO
tagline: Raw Sheep - Mitica - La Mancha, Spain
description: The producer of this raw milk Manchego makes cheese in a small town called Daimiel located near Las Tablas national park. He has won 15 awards and counting since 2001. The rind bears the traditional basket weave design, and is rubbed with olive oil during its 9-12 months of aging. This is an exceptional cheese - it is nutty, buttery and balanced with a sweet lingering finish. It is perfect enjoyed simply with cured meats, marcona almonds and dried fruit.

name: Manchego 1605
tagline: Raw Sheep - Finca Sierra la Solana/Essex St. Cheese Co. - La Mancha, Spain
description: Named to commemorate the year in which Don Quixote was written, Manchego 1605 is truly unique. This cheese is hand-selected for importation by the Essex St. Cheese Company. The folks at Essex focus mainly on flavor profile instead of a specific aging time. In this case, the criteria is sweetness and balance, avoiding the overly salted qualities of many manchegos. The waxless rind helps the cheese to breathe, resulting in a clean, sweet aroma of hay and almonds. Flavors are rustic and sheepy to start, giving way to a pleasant, milky sweetness with hints of warm spice.

name: Manchego 4 Month DO
tagline: Raw Sheep - Mitica - La Mancha, Spain
description: The producer of this raw milk Manchego makes cheese in a small town called Daimiel located near Las Tablas national park. He has won 15 awards and counting since 2001. Aged 4 months, the rind of this young Manchego bears the same destinctive basket weave design as its 12-month counterpart. Soft, milky and sweet, it has a mellow, lingering finish. It is perfect enjoyed simply with cured meats, marcona almonds and dried fruit.

name: Ossau Iraty Fermier AOP
tagline: Raw Sheep - Fermiers Basco Bearnais - Midi-Pyrenees, France
description: The Fermiers Basco-Béarnais Cooperative was created almost 40 years ago in the Aspe Valley, in the heart of the Béarnais Pyrenees. The Cooperative brings together nearly 20 farms that are all firmly committed to a centuries-old pastoral tradition, offering a range of 100% raw milk cheeses with a long ripening process, made by hand under the control of a technician, within collective salting rooms. Ossau Iraty is a wonderful sheep's milk cheese produced in a specific area of the French Pyrenées. The name is derived from the production area that includes two neighboring provinces: the Ossau Valley, located in the Bearn; and Iraty, a forested area in the French Basque Pyrenées. Traditionally served with black cherry jam, this farmstead Ossau Iraty can be readily paired with cured meats and a wide variety of wines.

name: Pantaleo
tagline: Pasteurized Goat - Latteria Sociale Santadi, Sardinia
description: Pantaleo is a unique goat’s milk cheese from Sardinia with very limited production. Aged a minimum of 100 days, it is made with milk from the Capra Sarda goat. The paste is ivory-colored with a pale rind and a sweet and clean floral finish. The off-dry texture makes it perfect to shave on salads or roasted vegetables, but its interesting flavor profile also make it perfect for a cheese plate.

name: Petit Agour Brebis
tagline: Pasteurized Sheep - Agour - Basque, France
description: Agour is a family owned and operated business in the heart of the Basque region of France. Petit Brebis is a pasteruized sheep's milk cheese with a smooth, creamy paste and a sweet, nutty flavor. Aromas are mild and pleasant with hints of roasted nuts. The distinctive orange rind is the result of it being rubbed with crushed espelette pepper during aging. It provides a vibrant color without affecting the flavor of the cheese.

name: Pyrenees Brebis
tagline: Pasteurized Sheep - Mons Fromagerie - Aquitaine, France
description: Pyrénées Brebis is an amazing cheese - but more for its subtlely than its assertiveness. Made in the forested area in the French Basque Pyrénées and aged by renowned affineur Herve Mons, this sheep's milk cheese is nutty and rich with a uniformly smooth and creamy texture. It is at once full flavored and accessible. The perfect choice for both the most adventurous and cautious of cheese lovers.

name: Ricotta Salata
tagline: Pasteurized Sheep - Mitica - Sardegna, Italy
description: This ricotta starts off with fresh sheep’s milk whey, which is pressed, salted and then aged to achieve its firm texture and briny taste. Similar to feta, Ricotta Salata is excellent crumbled, sliced into salads or grated over pasta. Often overlooked, this cheese is a cooking staple!

name: Tomme Brulee
tagline: Pasteurized Sheep - Pascal Beillevaire - Midi-Pyrenees, France
description: This is a remarkable cheese. Made in the Midi-Pyrenees region of Southwest France, it is aged by famed affineur Pascal Beillevaire. It has an impossibly smooth, creamy, golden/ivory paste with a nutty and sweet flavor. If an amazing texture and flavor wasn't enough, the rind is torched in the same way as the top of the famous dessert Creme Brulee. The result is a striking black and brown mottled rind - presentation is everything!

name: Wonderland
tagline: Raw Goat - Mountain Lodge Farm - Eatonville, WA
description: Nestled in the Cascade foothills, Mountain Lodge Farm hand-makes a variety of amazing cheeses. Wonderland, their take on a classic mountain tomme, is named for the beautiful trail that encircles Mt. Rainier. Made with raw goat's milk, Wonderland is rich, nutty, floral, and fruity. Its texture is firm but yielding with an eggshell colored paste. Perfect for snacking with salame and olives, it's also firm enough to shave on a salad or grate over roasted vegetables.
